title: Shared QINCo residual generator with stage Views
hypothesis: One shared official-structure QINCoStep plus tiny per-stage Givens coordinates on the decoded prefix will preserve fresh-world ANN recall while reducing the serialized model+index payload by at least 25% versus independently parameterized QINCo stages, and beat matched additive FiLM conditioning.
physical_object: One QINCo residual codebook generator (codebook, MLPconcat and residual blocks) shared across residual stages, plus one first-stage codebook.
mirror_coordinate: One scalar stage angle m_s; rotate adjacent pairs of the current decoded prefix before passing it as QINCoStep's conditioning vector.
logical_multiplicity: M-1 logical residual-stage generators from one physical QINCoStep.

dataset.generation: Each world samples new Gaussian cluster centers and anisotropic noise; train/database/query vectors are disjoint draws. Exact L2 top-10 on the raw database is the retrieval target.

controls: native QINCo with independent stage generators, using official QINCo v1 source structure
hard-tied single QINCoStep across all residual stages
shared QINCoStep plus per-stage Givens Mirror coordinate
shared QINCoStep plus same-size additive stage coordinate / rank-1 FiLM basis

training.initialization: stagewise torch k-means residual codebooks; identical seed/world per method
training.selection: No hyperparameter search; fixed settings are validated on development seed 103500.

metrics.storage: actual self-describing float32 model payload plus packed 4-bit-per-stage database code stream and ID/shape metadata
metrics.timing_method: Warm model path once; database encode is the median of 5 complete encodes; database decode-at-load and full 128-query scan are each medians of 20 complete repeats. Report load+scan throughput separately from scan-only throughput.

paid_objects: every trained codebook and generator tensor
deterministically_reconstructible_free: decoded database vectors, which are generated at load time from paid model plus paid codes; charge peak RAM and load compute

success_gate: Across all three fresh worlds, Mirror Recall@10 is no more than 0.02 below independent QINCo; it beats matched additive control by at least 0.01 Recall@10; total serialized model+index bytes are at least 25% lower than independent QINCo; and decode-at-load plus scan latency is no more than 10% slower than native QINCo.
failure_gate: Mirror fails any quality/byte/runtime gate, hard tying matches its quality at lower bytes, or additive conditioning matches/beats Mirror at similar payload.
boundaries: not SIFT/BigANN or large-scale ANN evidence
amendments: A1: the first development screen used single-shot encode/decode/scan timing, which showed unstable sub-millisecond differences. Before audit access, keep the same model and quality gates but warm up and use repeat medians for 5 encodes and 20 decode/scan runs. Preserve the initial timing artifact; see AMENDMENTS.md.
